$schema: LLM pricing history data — Tab 4 (Pricing History)

baseline.description: BenchLM's frontier token price index uses GPT-4's March 2023 launch price as index value 100. As of 2026-09-14 the index stood at 16 — an 84% drop in frontier pricing over roughly 3.5 years.

notes: Curated launch-price and price-cut milestones, not continuous daily data, per the onboarding spec. Prices are as originally announced at each date, not today's price (see the Pricing Comparison tab for current rates). Some pre-2025 figures come from third-party aggregator sites rather than the original provider announcement and could not be independently cross-checked against a primary source — those are flagged in their own 'notes' field; treat them as reasonably-sourced rather than verified. A number of milestones were found or corrected by scrubbing the Wayback Machine / Internet Archive (web.archive.org) for archived snapshots of each provider's own pricing pages — those entries cite the specific archived URL/timestamp used as evidence, and are treated as primary-source-equivalent since they're direct captures of the provider's own page, not a third party's summary of it.

milestones.notes: Launched with a single blended rate ($0.002/1K tokens), not separate input/output pricing.
Anchor point (index = 100) for BenchLM's frontier token price index. Confirmed directly via TechCrunch's launch-day coverage ($0.03/$0.06 per 1K tokens).

Not directly confirmed for the July 2023 launch itself, but InfoQ's coverage of the Claude 2.1 update (Nov 2023) confirms this exact rate ($8/$24 per million) was still in effect for the 2.1 point release, and Anthropic did not typically reprice minor version bumps — reasonable but not certain evidence the launch price was the same.
3x cheaper input / 2x cheaper output than original GPT-4 (8K). Confirmed directly via OpenAI's own DevDay announcement post ($0.01/$0.03 per 1K tokens).

Caveat found while cross-checking: Google's own launch post ('It's time for developers and enterprises to build with Gemini Pro') describes billing as 'per 1,000 characters or per image,' not per token. The $0.50/$1.50-per-million-tokens figure may be a later token-equivalent conversion rather than what was literally announced at launch — worth flagging if this milestone is presented as a direct quote.

Announced as a free research preview on this date, not with paid pricing. Paid/GA pricing followed in May 2024 (see next entry) — kept as a separate milestone since it's the actual announcement date most sources cite, but don't pair this date with the $3.50/$10.50 price.

Rate for prompts <=128K tokens. Confirmed via a dedicated Gemini pricing-history writeup (zerlo.net) cross-checked against Google's own Oct 2024 price-cut post, whose stated 64%/52% cut percentages are consistent with this starting price.
Rate for prompts <=128K tokens. A steep cut from its May 2024 launch price within about 3 months.

Rate for prompts <=128K tokens. Google's own blog post (developers.googleblog.com) confirms this date and states a '64% price reduction on input tokens, a 52% price reduction on output tokens' — consistent with the $3.50/$10.50 starting price above ($3.50 x 0.36 = $1.26 ~= $1.25; $10.50 x 0.48 = $5.04 ~= $5.00).
Launched alongside Claude 3 Sonnet and Claude 3 Haiku the same day.
4x cheaper than original GPT-4 at comparable or better quality.

Rate for prompts <=128K tokens. Sources disagree on the output figure: a dedicated Gemini pricing-history writeup (zerlo.net) says $0.53, while another aggregator we used earlier said $1.05 — going with $0.53 since that source explicitly frames it as the documented initial paid price, but this one is worth double-checking before treating as final.
Same price as Claude 3 Sonnet despite the capability jump.
~200x cheaper than GPT-4's original 2023 pricing.
50% input / 33% output cut from the May 2024 launch price, attributed to competitive pressure. Confirmed via TechCrunch/the-decoder coverage of the announcement.

A price *increase* despite the 'Haiku' (budget) branding — 4x more than Claude 3 Haiku's $0.25/$1.25, justified by Anthropic as reflecting that 3.5 Haiku surpassed the older Claude 3 Opus on many benchmarks. Confirmed via TechCrunch coverage.

A 20% across-the-board cut from the Nov 2024 launch price, found via Wayback Machine archives rather than a press announcement — a 2025-02-03 archived snapshot of anthropic.com/pricing shows this rate, and the page's own CMS metadata timestamps the pricing card's last edit at 2024-12-03T03:49:45Z. Cache write also cut $1.25->$1.00/M and cache read $0.125->$0.08/M. Not previously recorded in this dataset.

Launch price, per Anthropic's own announcement post ("Pricing is now $5/$25 per million tokens") — there was no earlier Claude Opus 4.5 price to cut from. Anthropic's post doesn't itself frame this against prior Opus pricing, but it lands 67% below the $15/$75 Opus rate that had held since Claude 3 Opus's March 2024 launch and carried through Opus 4 / 4.1 unchanged; that chain is now directly confirmed via archived anthropic.com/docs pricing tables (Opus 3, 4, and 4.1 all showing $15/$75 as of a 2025-11-19 snapshot), not just outlet headlines as previously noted. This is the price point today's Opus 5 still uses.

First real cut to the Sonnet tier's price in this dataset — Sonnet had held at $3/$15 since Claude 3 Sonnet's March 2024 launch straight through 3.5, 3.7, 4, and 4.5, now directly confirmed via archived docs.anthropic.com pricing tables (a 2025-05-12 snapshot shows 3/3.5/3.7 at $3/$15; a 2025-11-19 snapshot shows 4/4.5 at $3/$15). A 'Sonnet 4.6' is mentioned in some third-party aggregator tracking as part of this unbroken chain, but no archived snapshot through Nov 2025 shows such a model existing — treat its existence as unconfirmed rather than assuming it held the same price. Introductory/launch pricing, explicitly framed by Anthropic as temporary at the time (see the Aug 2026 entry below).

Anthropic had scheduled Sonnet 5's introductory $2/$10 rate to rise 50% to $3/$15 on September 1, 2026, but cancelled the hike on this date and made $2/$10 permanent instead. Worth knowing for Tab 4: this is the one entry in the dataset where a price move went the *other* way from what was announced. Separately, Sonnet 5 uses a new tokenizer that produces roughly 30% more tokens than Sonnet 4.6 for the same text — so real-world workload cost may have effectively risen ~30% even though the rate card didn't move.

Rate for prompts <=200k tokens (>200k rises to $2.50/$15.00); cached input $0.125/M. Entered experimental testing ~March 2025, public preview on Vertex AI from April 9, then GA on this date. Previously missing from this dataset entirely — an untracked model generation between Gemini 2.0 Flash (Dec 2024) and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview (Feb 2026). Price is the currently-listed rate; not independently re-verified via an archived GA-day snapshot, so treat the exact launch-day figure as reasonably-sourced rather than certain.

Cached input $0.03/M. In preview since April 17, 2025; GA'd alongside Gemini 2.5 Pro at Google I/O 2025. Previously missing from this dataset entirely. Price is the currently-listed rate, not independently re-verified via an archived GA-day snapshot.

Cached input $0.01/M. Released as a stable version for developers and enterprise builders on this date. Previously missing from this dataset entirely. Price is the currently-listed rate, not independently re-verified via an archived launch-day snapshot.

Rate for prompts <=200k tokens; cached input $0.20/M. Launched at the exact same price Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview still uses today — 3.1 was a model bump at flat pricing, not a repricing of 3, confirmed via archive.org snapshots of ai.google.dev showing 3 Pro Preview at this rate through its Mar 9, 2026 retirement/redirect to 3.1. Previously missing from this dataset entirely.

Batch API $0.25/$1.50; cached input $0.05/M. Previously missing from this dataset entirely — the mid-tier counterpart to Gemini 3 Pro Preview's Nov 2025 launch. Price is the currently/recently-listed rate per third-party trackers (tokencost, pricepertoken), not independently re-verified via an archived launch-day snapshot.

Rate for prompts <=200k tokens, same as the current listed rate — no price cut on record since launch. Launch date confirmed directly via Google's own announcement post (blog.google/.../gemini-3-1-pro/), which doesn't itself state pricing; the price comes from ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing.

Same list price as the current listed rate — no price cut on record since launch. Sourced directly from Google's own announcement post (blog.google/.../gemini-3-6-flash-3-5-flash-lite-3-5-flash-cyber/).

Introductory rate (same announcement as Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite above), matching the current listed rate; list price of $1.50/$7.50 applies starting Jan 1, 2027 per the same announcement. Previously missing from this dataset entirely, despite being the direct predecessor Gemini 3.7 Flash was benchmarked against three weeks later. Sourced directly from Google's own announcement post (blog.google/.../gemini-3-6-flash-3-5-flash-lite-3-5-flash-cyber/), corroborated by press coverage (9to5Google) confirming the Dec 31, 2026 introductory-pricing cutoff.

Introductory rate, described by Google as a 50% discount versus Gemini 3.6 Flash's $1.50/$7.50 list price; same $1.50/$7.50 list price applies to this model too starting Jan 1, 2027. Previously missing from this dataset entirely. Sourced via press coverage (VentureBeat, 9to5Google, Android Headlines) of Google's own announcement.

Introductory rate, matching the current listed rate; set to rise to $1.50/$7.50 on Jan 1, 2027 per the same announcement. Sourced directly from Google's own announcement post (blog.google/.../3-8-flash-and-3-8-flash-cyber/).

Frontier-class benchmark results at budget pricing — this release is widely credited with triggering the 'DeepSeek moment' repricing pressure across the industry in early 2025. Figures shown are the list/sticker price; a launch-day introductory discount actually billed at $0.14 input / $0.28 output through ~2025-02-07 (see the Feb 2025 entry below), confirmed via an archived 2024-12-26 snapshot of api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing showing the list prices struck through next to the discounted ones.
Cache-miss input price shown ($0.55/M); cache-hit input was $0.14/M. Sourced directly from DeepSeek's own release announcement (api-docs.deepseek.com).

The launch-day introductory discount ($0.14/$0.28 effective price) expired, reverting to the $0.27/$1.10 list price that had been on the rate card since Dec 2024 but not actually charged. Archived snapshots pin this to between 2025-02-07 (still discounted) and 2025-02-09 (discount gone) — exact day not independently confirmed. Not previously recorded in this dataset.

Standard price unchanged; DeepSeek introduced its first off-peak discount scheme alongside the Feb 2025 repricing above — 50% off during 16:30-00:30 UTC each day. This is the structural precedent for the peak/off-peak split later applied to the V4 family (Aug 2026). Confirmed via archived api-docs.deepseek.com pricing table footnote. Not previously recorded in this dataset.

Standard price unchanged; same Feb 2025 repricing introduced a 75% off-peak discount for R1 (steeper than V3's 50%) during 16:30-00:30 UTC each day. Confirmed via archived api-docs.deepseek.com pricing table footnote. Not previously recorded in this dataset.

Covers both deepseek-chat (V3.1 non-thinking) and deepseek-reasoner (V3.1 thinking) — DeepSeek-V3.1 itself had released 2025-08-21 without a pricing change of its own. Effective 16:00 UTC this date, DeepSeek unified chat/reasoner onto one flat rate ($0.07 cache-hit / $0.56 cache-miss / $1.68 output) and explicitly cancelled the Feb 2025 nighttime discount scheme for both models. Confirmed via DeepSeek's own pricing-page announcement text. Not previously recorded in this dataset.

A 50-60% cut from the Sept 5 unified V3.1 rate ($0.56/$1.68) at launch. Cache-hit input $0.028/M. Renamed to GA as 'DeepSeek-V3.2' on 2025-12-01 with no further price change. Confirmed via DeepSeek's own release post (api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news250929/). Not previously recorded in this dataset.

Real launch date and list price — corrects a prior version of this dataset, which mistakenly recorded this model's launch as 2026-08-13 at $0.435/$0.87 (that was actually a later promotional rate, see entries below; 2026-08-13 was just a same-priced version-tag bump to 'V4-Pro-0813' immediately preceding the real Aug 16 price hike). Cache-hit input $0.145/M at launch, no peak/off-peak split yet. Launched alongside DeepSeek-V4-Flash (see separate entry). Confirmed via archived api-docs.deepseek.com pricing snapshots.

Real launch date and price — corrects a prior version of this dataset, which mistakenly recorded this model's launch as 2026-09-10 at $0.15/$0.60 (that was actually a later rename+reprice to 'DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash', see entry below). Cache-hit input $0.028/M at launch, flat rate with no peak/off-peak split yet. Confirmed via archived api-docs.deepseek.com pricing snapshots.

At 12:15 UTC: a permanent 10x cut to cache-hit pricing across the V4 family, plus a limited-time 75% promotional discount on V4-Pro specifically (initially through 05/05, later extended to 05/31 — see next entry) that brought the effective rate here to $0.435/$0.87. This is the number a prior version of this dataset mistakenly labeled as the model's launch price. Confirmed via archived api-docs.deepseek.com pricing snapshots.

At 15:59 UTC, per a 2026-05-22 announcement, the Apr 26 promotional 75%-off rate became the permanent official price rather than reverting to the $1.74/$3.48 list price. No numeric change from the entry above — flagging the status change (temporary -> permanent) since it's what made $0.435/$0.87 the durable 'current' rate before the Aug 16 hike. Confirmed via a 2026-06-02 archived snapshot showing no discount/strikethrough language.

Off-peak rate shown, introduced alongside V4-Pro's Aug 16 hike (see next entry); peak hours double everything to $0.44/$1.32. Up from the flat $0.14/$0.28 launch rate. Confirmed via archived api-docs.deepseek.com pricing snapshots. Not previously recorded in this dataset.

A steep hike from the $0.435/$0.87 rate that had been permanent since May 31, introduced alongside a new peak/off-peak split — off-peak rate shown here (matches the current listed rate); peak hours (01:00-04:00 & 06:00-10:00 UTC, Mon-Fri) double everything to $1.32 input / $3.96 output. Confirmed via DeepSeek's own announcement, corroborated by multiple outlets (Engadget, InfoWorld, Qz) reporting increases 'up to 1,100%' on some token types.

Off-peak rate, matching the current listed rate for this model; peak doubles everything to $0.30/$1.20. A prior version of this dataset recorded this as 'DeepSeek-V4-Flash' launching on this date at this price — DeepSeek's own docs now confirm this is actually a rename: the 'DeepSeek-V4-Flash' model ID (which really launched 2026-04-24, see that entry) was retired on this date, with requests redirected to this new 'DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash' model under a new 'deepseek-flash' API name, at a cut price (down from $0.22/$0.66 off-peak). This resolves a naming discrepancy an earlier version of this dataset had flagged as unresolved.
Cached input priced separately at $0.125/M. Priced low enough that press coverage described it as risking a renewed price war. Sourced directly from TechCrunch's launch-day coverage.

Same list price as Claude 3.5 Haiku's Dec 2024 cut, and matches the current listed rate — no price cut on record since launch. Launched a few weeks after Claude Sonnet 4.5. Previously missing from this dataset entirely; confirmed via CNBC's launch-day coverage and Anthropic's own announcement post (anthropic.com/news/claude-haiku-4-5), with the archived pricing page also showing this rate in effect by 2025-11-19.
Same list price as the current listed rate — no price cut on record since launch. Sourced directly from Mistral's own announcement post (mistral.ai/news/mistral-3/), published 2025-12-02.
Same list price as the current listed rate — no price cut on record since launch. Sourced directly from Mistral's own announcement post (mistral.ai/news/mistral-small-4/).

Same list price as the current listed rate — no price cut on record since launch. The dedicated launch post wasn't directly accessible while compiling this dataset; date and price are corroborated by Mistral's own docs model card (docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-medium-3-5-26-04) and independent coverage (Winbuzzer), which agree with each other.

Sourced directly from OpenAI's own GPT-5.6 announcement post. Cut to $4.00/$20.00 on 2026-08-21 (see price-cut entry below), which is what the Sept 2026 blended-price cut recorded further below was actually tracking — not a cached-input change as this note previously speculated.

Sourced directly from OpenAI's own GPT-5.6 announcement post. Cut to $2.00/$12.00 by Sept 2026 (see price-cut entry below) — a 20% reduction on both input and output, consistent with BenchLM's reported 20% blended-price cut.

Sourced directly from OpenAI's own GPT-5.6 announcement post. Cut to $0.20/$1.20 by Sept 2026 (see price-cut entry below) — an 80% reduction on both input and output, consistent with BenchLM's reported 80% blended-price cut (the largest in their latest ledger).

First xAI entry in this dataset, which previously had zero history before Aug 2026. Launched alongside a $300/month consumer subscription tier. Sourced from TechCrunch's launch-day coverage, corroborated by independent pricing trackers (eesel, mem0). xAI's own launch post (x.ai/news/grok-4) didn't scrape cleanly for a direct primary-source price quote, so this is press-confirmed rather than screenshot-verified.

Announced 2025-09-19, released 2025-09-23. Rate shown is for short-context requests; long-context (above the model's threshold) doubles to $0.40 input / $1.00 output. Sourced directly from xAI's own announcement post (x.ai/news/grok-4-fast), which scraped cleanly with a matching pricing table.

~40% cheaper input / ~60% cheaper output than its Grok 4.20 predecessor, per Artificial Analysis. No first-party xAI announcement post surfaced for this release — it appears to have been a quiet catalog release established via third-party trackers and resold inference endpoints rather than a formal launch (VentureBeat covered it as 'an aggressively low price' launch). Confirmed present and unchanged in xAI's official docs/migration pages as of the May 2026 retirement below.

At 12:00 PM PT, xAI retired grok-4-0709 (original Grok 4), grok-4-fast (both reasoning and non-reasoning), grok-3, and grok-code-fast-1, silently redirecting all remaining traffic to grok-4.3 billing. For Grok 4 Fast callers this was an effective price *increase* of roughly 525% on input / 400% on output (from $0.20/$0.50 to $1.25/$2.50) with no model change on their end beyond the billing switch. Confirmed directly via xAI's own migration-guide page (docs.x.ai/developers/migration/may-15-retirement), which explicitly states callers 'will be billed at grok-4.3 pricing of $1.25 per 1M input tokens and $2.50 per 1M output tokens.' Not previously recorded in this dataset.

API launch 2026-07-08; consumer rollout followed 2026-07-22. A price *increase* from Grok 4.3's $1.25/$2.50 — breaks this dataset's usual 'prices only fall' pattern. Sourced directly from xAI's own announcement post (x.ai/news/grok-4-5): 'Grok 4.5 is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens.' Same price Grok 4.6 and 4.7 both later launched at.

Rate shown is for short-context requests (under the model's 200k-token long-context threshold); above that, all rates double. Superseded by Grok 4.7 on 2026-09-21 at the identical list price (see launch entry below) — no price cut on record for this model before it was replaced. Sourced directly from xAI's own announcement post (x.ai/news/grok-4-6).

Same list price as Grok 4.6 despite a larger base model and longer RL training cycle — xAI's own announcement explicitly called out the unchanged pricing. Rate shown is for short-context requests (under the 200k-token long-context threshold); above that, all rates double to $4.00 input / $12.00 output (cached input: $0.50 short-context / $1.00 long-context). Matches the current listed rate. Sourced directly from xAI's own announcement, corroborated by press coverage (MarkTechPost, the-decoder) confirming the identical $2/$6 pricing.

Launched at roughly 2.5x GPT-5.6 Sol's list price. Rate shown is for prompts <=272,000 tokens (1.05M token context window); above that threshold pricing rises to $20 input / $75 output. Cached input priced separately at $1/M (90% off base), cache writes at $12.50/M. OpenAI's own pricing page returned a 403 while compiling this dataset, so this is cross-checked against OpenAI's launch announcement post and multiple independent trackers (Yotta Labs, Layer3 Labs, AiCybr) that all agree on these figures.
Blended rate is BenchLM's figure, not Anthropic's — BenchLM's index tracks a single blended rate per model rather than separate input/output figures.

20% input cut / 33% output cut from the $5.00/$30.00 launch price ($0.50->$0.40 cached input too); matches the current listed rate. This is the actual sticker-price event the Sept 14 blended-price entry below was tracking (0.75*input + 0.25*output reproduces both the $11.25/M launch and $8.00/M post-cut blended figures exactly) — not a cached-input-only change as earlier notes in this file speculated. Confirmed as promotional pricing in effect through 2026-11-21T23:59 UTC (exact expiration timestamp per OpenAI's own pricing-page embedded data, found via a 2026-09-09 archive.org snapshot). Sourced from OpenAI's own developer community announcement ('20% price reduction for GPT 5.6 Sol'), corroborated by citybiz coverage, and verified live on developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (checked 2026-09-23).

BenchLM's change-ledger figure (blended $11.25/M -> $8.00/M, 28.9% decrease) for the same Aug 21 sticker-price cut recorded directly above — BenchLM just recorded it a few weeks later. Blended figure, not directly comparable to the separate input/output rates tracked elsewhere in this dataset.
Cut from a blended $5.63/M to $4.50/M (20% decrease), per BenchLM's change ledger.
Cut from a blended $2.25/M to $0.45/M (80% decrease) — the largest single cut in BenchLM's latest change-ledger snapshot.
84% below the March 2023 GPT-4 baseline (index = 100). This is the single number that best tells Tab 4's overall story: frontier LLM pricing has fallen by roughly 6x since GPT-4's original launch.
